picks.crowd_contradiction: OLBG's most-tipped selection for this match is Karen Khachanov, on two tips out of two. Our originated line makes Carlos Alcaraz a 68% favourite. This is the single largest crowd-versus-evidence divergence in the whole capture and is published on the Flagged page.
corroboration: Official ATP standings have Alcaraz third on 5,610 points against Khachanov 24th on 2,030.

Alcaraz has three titles in 2026 - the Australian Open, where he beat Novak Djokovic in the final, the Qatar Open at Doha and the Japan Open at Tokyo - and has already qualified for the ATP Finals.
Khachanov is 30 and has won seven tour titles across a career in which he has never beaten this opponent.
counter_arguments: Alcaraz is returning to Vienna for the first time since 2021 and has had a wrist problem this season that cost him the French Open entirely and kept him out for several months.

Khachanov's 2026 US Open result is recorded inconsistently across sources - one lists him as the champion, two others as a semi-finalist - so his current form cannot be stated with confidence. That unresolved question is precisely why the prior here is held below what a 6-0 head-to-head alone would justify.
Only two OLBG tips exist on this match, which is far too thin a sample to treat as evidence for either side.
picks.prediction: Carlos Alcaraz opens his Vienna campaign against Karen Khachanov on the indoor hard courts, returning to this tournament for the first time since 2021 with three titles already banked in 2026 - the Australian Open, Doha and Tokyo. The official rankings separate them by 21 places and more than 3,500 points, and Alcaraz has won all six previous meetings between them without dropping a match. Khachanov is a seven-time tour champion and a real indoor player, and Alcaraz's wrist has troubled him this year, so this is not a walkover. Even so, the OLBG crowd backing Khachanov on two tips is nowhere near enough to shift the case. Back Alcaraz to win.
